summary: We researched a variety of physical characteristics of Mars such as elevation, geology, topography, erosion and then chose a variety of sites that are similar. Each site we chose corresponds to a different characteristic of Mars e.g. the Afar depression is topographically and geologically similar to the Valles Marineris however is not similar in temperature. The steep cliffs can be used to model a test landing of a rover and the volcanic terrain can be used to test the functionality of wheels or tracks. Unfortunately a perfect analogue of Mars on Earth is impossible, so by combining the sites hopefully an overall analogue will be created.
details:
Our project investigates the geological characteristics of Mars and explores how different environments on Earth can be used as analogues to better understand the Martian surface.

We researched locations on Mars, examining their geological composition, topography, mineralogy, climate and geological history. We then compare these characteristics with suitable Earth locations, such as the Afar Depression in Ethiopia and the Red Desert in Wyoming to identify similarities and differences in their geological structures and formation processes.

The project demonstrates how studying environments on Earth can help scientists understand geological processes on Mars. This could contribute to Martian exploration by helping researchers identify locations of scientific interest and understand the challenges that potential exploration sites might present. Additionally, these analogues could be used again for future missions on other planets.

We used many tools to search for sites, most notably NASA earthdata, worldview and Mars Trek along with scientific papers on the volcanism and terrain of Mars.

The creative aspect is identifying different sites all around the world. There are tens of thousands of different enviroments in the world and choosing a couple requires lots of creativity.

We considered factors such as: geology, mineral composition, weather, temperatures, terrain, topography and elevation to make our decisions.

All pictures of bidoof were used with permission
